scope: source-grounded matrix of necessary, supporting and non-identifying observables; no new experiment or EDF run
course_status: Day27 uncredited preview only; Day28 unopened

matrix.quantity: T, Rz(pi), T Ry(pi) residual on j(r)

MR.necessary: Only as a self-consistency/model check after density, axis convention and occupied configuration are fixed.
MR.supporting: A planar TAC solution may preserve a combined antiunitary signature while breaking separate T; a self-consistent current pattern can support the shears geometry.
MR.not_identifiable: 017/034 arbitrary Gaussian residuals cannot assign MR or distinguish it from another current-carrying configuration.

AMR.necessary: A specified double-shears calculation must show the intended transverse cancellation and symmetry relation.
AMR.supporting: Opposite blade/current contributions can support cancellation of a chosen transverse moment.
AMR.not_identifiable: Zero integrated moment or a local residual does not prove AMR, pointwise zero current, or vanishing all M1 matrix elements.

matrix.quantity: DCO/IPDCO, angular correlations, ΔI sequence and crossover assignments

MR.necessary: Necessary to establish that the candidate band contains ΔI=1 M1-dominated links and identify E2 crossovers before extracting strengths.
MR.supporting: Regular ΔI=1 M1 links with weak crossover E2 are consistent with shears rotation.
MR.not_identifiable: Multipolarity alone cannot separate MR from other dipole bands or configuration mixing.

AMR.necessary: Necessary to verify the regular ΔI=2 E2 candidate and identify any allowed cross-band M1/E1 links.
AMR.supporting: A clean ΔI=2 E2 sequence is compatible with the ideal double-shears picture.
AMR.not_identifiable: Absence of ΔI=2 M1 follows general selection rules and is not AMR-specific.

matrix.locator: Hübel 2005 pp.22-31,55-57; Frauendorf 2001 p.488; Agarwal 2007 PDF pp.3-7

MR.necessary: Needed for a quantitative shears-strength and g-factor comparison; relative ratios alone are underdetermined.
MR.supporting: Large or spin-evolving B(M1), often decreasing toward blade closure, supports MR with configuration context.
MR.not_identifiable: A large B(M1) is not unique to MR; without lifetime the absolute numerator is unknown.

AMR.necessary: Not a universal requirement for every candidate, but absolute M1 limits/values are needed to test transverse cancellation against alternatives.
AMR.supporting: Small intraband transverse M1 within a specified double-shears model supports AMR.
AMR.not_identifiable: No measured ΔI=2 M1 line cannot prove AMR; cross-band M1 can remain allowed.

matrix.locator: Hübel 2005 HU05-1/HU05-AR-1; Agarwal 2007 AG07-5; antimagnetic-rotation boundary page

MR.necessary: Needed with B(M1) to quantify weak core collectivity and separate shears from core rotation.
MR.supporting: Weak or slowly changing E2 crossover supports a weakly deformed magnetic band.
MR.not_identifiable: Weak B(E2) also occurs in termination, weak collectivity and band mixing.

AMR.necessary: Needed to test the predicted E2 evolution with spin; requires lifetime/branching and configuration checks.
AMR.supporting: Small/decreasing B(E2) in a regular ΔI=2 sequence supports AMR.
AMR.not_identifiable: No universal sin⁴ law or numerical threshold applies when core E2, shape and configuration vary.

matrix.locator: Roy 2011 RO11-1 p.324 Table 1; Frauendorf 2001 p.488; Hübel 2005 pp.55-57

MR.necessary: Useful comparative observable after both absolute or consistently derived strengths are identified.
MR.supporting: Large/evolving ratios can support magnetic dominance and crossing structure.
MR.not_identifiable: A ratio cannot determine whether M1 increased or E2 decreased; Agarwal 2007 explicitly lacks absolute lifetimes.

AMR.necessary: Not sufficient or mandatory alone; must be paired with E2 lifetimes, ΔI structure and configuration.
AMR.supporting: A large ratio may indicate weak E2 in an AMR candidate, but its units and response are source-dependent.
AMR.not_identifiable: It is not dimensionless and has no universal ≥100 hard gate.

MR.necessary: No; it helps locate alignment/crossing and must be interpreted with configuration and transition data.
MR.supporting: Smooth or anomalous response can support a TAC crossing interpretation.
MR.not_identifiable: A J^(2) extremum alone does not establish shears or a 3qp→5qp causal chain.

AMR.necessary: No; it is a kinematic response, not a mode label.
AMR.supporting: Large J^(2) relative to measured B(E2) is a comparative clue in AMR systematics.
AMR.not_identifiable: J^(2)/B(E2) cannot be used as a universal unitless discriminator.

matrix.locator: Frauendorf 2001 F01-3/F01-11; Roy 2011 RO11-4 and RO11-D26C-004

MR.necessary: Necessary for robust M1/E2 assignment in many in-beam datasets.
MR.supporting: M1 character and E2 crossover assignment support the candidate band.
MR.not_identifiable: Polarization does not measure an intrinsic current field or prove shears closure.

AMR.necessary: Necessary to identify E2 sequence and constrain competing M1/E1 links.
AMR.supporting: Consistent E2 character supports the candidate transition network.
AMR.not_identifiable: Polarization alone cannot distinguish AMR from a termination or ordinary weak E2 band.

MR.necessary: Needed to convert intensities to absolute B(M1), B(E2) and test model geometry quantitatively.
MR.supporting: Consistent lifetimes across a band strengthen the transition-systematics chain.
MR.not_identifiable: A lifetime measurement without secure band identity/configuration does not assign MR.

AMR.necessary: Needed for absolute E2 evolution and to test cancellation models; source-dependent method choice is allowed.
AMR.supporting: A reliable B(E2) decline or plateau pattern supports a specified AMR/core-coupling model.
AMR.not_identifiable: A single lifetime or an absent shift cannot by itself prove AMR.

matrix.locator: Hübel 2005 pp.22-31,55-57; Roy 2011 pp.322-326; antimagnetic-rotation page

matrix.quantity: high-j particle/hole assignment, i_x, band crossings, max-spin path

MR.necessary: Necessary for the shears interpretation and for distinguishing core rotation, signature partners and crossing.
MR.supporting: Alignment additivity and a source-consistent TAC configuration support MR.
MR.not_identifiable: Configuration labels inferred only from a fit or one energy trend are not unique.

AMR.necessary: Necessary to establish two coupled blades and account for core angular momentum.
AMR.supporting: Finite-core coupling and a Pauli-consistent termination path support AMR.
AMR.not_identifiable: A guessed blade Jmax or termination point cannot be transferred across nuclei.

matrix.locator: Clark 2000 CL00-4/5; Roy 2011 RO11-2/3; Olbratowski 2002 model-boundary

MR.necessary: Useful for regularity and crossing maps, but not a standalone requirement.
MR.supporting: Smooth ΔI=1 behavior can support a candidate sequence.
MR.not_identifiable: Near-degeneracy or smooth S(I) cannot distinguish MR from chirality, wobbling or signature partners.

AMR.necessary: Regular ΔI=2 level sequence is a candidate-level structural input.
AMR.supporting: Smooth rotational-like energies support the geometric model when EM data agree.
AMR.not_identifiable: Energy regularity alone cannot separate AMR from termination or weak collective rotation.

toy_input_status: 017/034 fields are arbitrary Gaussian current constructions; 031 is conditional frozen-gyro arithmetic. They provide unit/symmetry self-checks only.
global_conclusion: MR and AMR are configuration-dependent interpretations requiring a convergent evidence chain. No single current residual, multipolarity, B ratio, J2, polarization or lifetime is sufficient.
